items.title: Fourteen Candidates Register for Mississauga's October Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, a total of 14 candidates have registered to run for mayor of Mississauga in the city's October 26 municipal election. The outlet reports incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who won the seat in a 2024 byelection after decades as a city councillor and federal Liberal MP, is seeking to hold onto the position. CityNews Toronto reports polling from Liaison Strategies published August 14 suggests the race has narrowed to a head-to-head contest between Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. According to the outlet, Crombie served a decade as Mississauga's mayor before resigning in 2024 to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, then stepped down from that role after failing to win a seat in the 2025 provincial election. CityNews Toronto reports Crombie is now looking to return to her former job in what is expected to be a high-stakes race.

items.title: New Streetsville Secondary School Bus Route Joins MiWay's Back-to-School Lineup
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, MiWay has introduced a new secondary school bus route to help students get to class safely as the new school year begins. The city reports Route 305 Streetsville SS now operates between Meadowvale Village and Streetsville Secondary School. According to the city, MiWay's regular post-secondary and secondary school service has also resumed for the year, connecting students to schools, colleges and universities across Mississauga. The city says the transit system offers affordable fares and simple trip-planning tools aimed at making back-to-school travel safer and more convenient. According to the city, back-to-school season is one of the busiest times of year on the road, and officials are encouraging students and families to plan routes ahead of time.

items.title: Trump's Truth Social Threat Against Bombardier Sales Raises Stakes for Mississauga Plant
items.summary: According to INsauga, U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened to block Bombardier aircraft from the American market, a move that could have major implications for Mississauga, where the company has a significant manufacturing presence and is in the process of expanding its local operations. The outlet reports Trump made the threat in a Monday post on Truth Social, declaring there would be no more selling of Bombardier aircraft in the United States. INsauga reports the comments mark the latest escalation in the ongoing trade dispute between Canada and the United States. According to the outlet, Trump argued that Bombardier relies too heavily on the American market, claiming more than half of its revenue comes from the United States. INsauga reports the threat raises questions about where Bombardier's aircraft will ultimately be manufactured and what the fallout could mean for the company's Mississauga workforce.

items.title: Amherst Father and Son Face Life-Altering Injuries After Highway 403 Chain-Reaction Crash
items.summary: According to WKBW, a father and son from Amherst, New York suffered catastrophic injuries after a chain-reaction crash on Highway 403 in Mississauga on August 11. The outlet reports 43-year-old Masud Biswas and his 12-year-old son Marif had pulled onto the highway shoulder after a minor collision with another vehicle to exchange insurance information, when a third vehicle veered off course and struck the parked car, which then hit both of them. WKBW reports both were taken to trauma centres, and Masud has since had both legs amputated above the knee while recovering at Erie County Medical Center. According to the outlet, Marif, a seventh grader at Amherst Middle School, has undergone multiple surgeries as doctors work to save his legs and remains at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo. WKBW reports the family's neighbor, Matt Higgins, has launched a fundraising campaign to help cover their medical and living expenses while Masud, the family's main income earner, is unable to work.

items.title: Police Call Mississauga Stabbing an Isolated Incident as Search for Second Suspect Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police say the Mississauga stabbing that left one person fighting for their life is believed to be an isolated incident with no ongoing threat to public safety. The outlet reports one suspect was taken into custody at the scene while officers continued searching the surrounding area for a second suspect. INsauga reports police describe the outstanding suspect as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four, with blonde and brown hair. According to the outlet, the victim remained in critical condition at a trauma centre as of the latest police update. INsauga reports officers remained in the Main Street and Dundas Street East area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Proposed for Dixie Site Head to Planning Committee
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council approve a rezoning application that would bring two 16-storey apartment towers to a 3-acre site at 1225 Dundas Street East in the Dixie neighbourhood. The outlet reports the towers would be connected by a six-storey podium and contain a combined 553 residential rental units, along with ground-floor commercial space. Mississauga.com reports the proposal also includes 34 four-storey back-to-back townhouses, bringing the total to 587 residential units. According to the outlet, the site is owned by a group of five investment companies, including Stephen-Mitchell Realty Limited and Whitehorn Investments Limited. Mississauga.com reports a city staff report noted the property sits within a designated intensification area meant to accommodate significant growth, with Mississauga's planning committee set to vote on the application September 8.

items.title: City Says $401M Transit Funding Will Ease Capacity Crunch as MiWay Facilities Max Out
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city officials say more than $400 million in provincial and federal funding will help address a transit capacity crunch as MiWay's existing facilities operate at full capacity. The outlet reports the funding, which comes through the Development Charges Reduction Program, would support two major transit projects if approved. According to the outlet, the city anticipates transit ridership will grow by 50 per cent by 2035, a jump officials say would require an additional 250 buses. Mississauga.com reports the funding announcement was made by Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Premier Doug Ford and other government officials on September 3. According to the outlet, Mississauga secured the money after becoming one of the first Ontario cities to cut development charges by 100 per cent for certain types of housing to encourage growth.
